axes.would_differ: If the subject were broader (e.g., entire circulatory system), the plan would add vascular histology, blood pressure regulation, and lymphatic system. If narrower (e.g., only valves), chambers and vessels would be dropped.
If purpose were board exams, more descriptive text and fewer MCQ-oriented facts. If for clinical rotation, emphasis would shift to auscultation points, ECG correlates, and pathologies.

If the learner were a first-time biology student, the plan would need 4-5 foundational concepts (cell transport, epithelial tissue, basic circulation) before heart anatomy. If a medical student, it would skip NCERT basics and focus on clinical correlations.

verified.quote: i need to be able to label diagrams

axes.would_differ: If the target were 'explain cardiac cycle phases', the plan would add pressure-volume loops, Wiggers diagram, and valve timing. If 'solve NEET MCQs', it would add previous-year question patterns and common traps.
If a strict time limit were stated (e.g., '2 hours'), the plan would prioritize only the 15 highest-yield labels. If a page limit were stated, diagram density would increase.
axes.reason: never asked — Semantics §1 LOCKED — optional, and the corollary: deriving the plan and reporting its extent is what CAUSES a capacity to be stated. Asking upfront asks for a number the learner cannot honestly give.

axes.would_differ: If depth were 'conceptual mastery', the plan would include developmental embryology, electrophysiology, and hemodynamics. If 'minimal passing', only the 10 most-tested labels.
axes.reason: never asked — Semantics §1 — biasing, not binding. A default is always defensible.

axes.value: annotated diagram-focused study notes with labeling practice
axes.would_differ: If artifact were 'flashcards', the plan would output Q/A pairs per label. If 'video script', it would sequence visual reveals. If 'mind map', it would cluster by chamber/flow path.
If template were 'NCERT chapter summary', the output would follow textbook section order. If 'clinical anatomy atlas', it would use surgical views and cross-sections.

judgements.why: Standard NEET diagram labeling item; orientation questions appear regularly.
Surface anatomy and sulci identification tested in diagram-based MCQs.
Key structures (fossa ovalis, SA node, IVC/SVC openings, coronary sinus) are high-yield labeling targets.
Trabeculae, papillary muscles, moderator band, and pulmonary valve anatomy appear in cross-section diagrams.
Pulmonary vein openings and mitral valve orifice are tested in internal view diagrams.
Aortic vestibule, papillary muscles, and thick wall are standard labeling items.
Three cusps, chordae tendineae, and papillary muscle connections are diagram staples.
Semilunar valve structure and location in pulmonary trunk tested in diagrams.
Two cusps, chordae, and papillary muscles are high-yield for labeling.
Three semilunar cusps and coronary ostia origins are standard diagram items.
Annuli fibrosi and their role in valve anchoring and electrical insulation appear in theory MCQs.
SVC, IVC, and coronary sinus openings into RA are fundamental for blood flow tracing.
Pulmonary trunk bifurcation into left/right pulmonary arteries is a key flow pathway step.
Four pulmonary veins entering LA tested in both labeling and flow sequence questions.
Ascending aorta, arch, and major branches (brachiocephalic, left common carotid, left subclavian) appear in diagrams and flow questions.
RCA, LCA, LAD, LCX dominance and supply areas are high-yield theory and occasional diagram items.
Coronary sinus drainage into RA is a specific labeling point in posterior heart views.
Core competency: tracing deoxygenated → oxygenated pathway through all chambers, valves, and vessels is the primary stated target.
SA node, AV node, Bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fibers locations and functions are standard theory and occasional diagram items.

judgements.concept: Cardiac cycle phases and pressure changes
judgements.why: Pressure-volume loops, valve open/close timing, and phase definitions are high-yield theory for NEET.
S1/S2 correlation with valve closure is tested in theory MCQs.
P wave, QRS, T wave correlation with atrial/ventricular depolarization/repolarization is standard theory.
CO = HR × SV, stroke volume, ejection fraction definitions appear in numerical and conceptual MCQs.

judgements.concept: Autonomic regulation of heart rate and contractility
judgements.why: Sympathetic/parasympathetic effects on SA/AV nodes and contractility are theory staples.
Heart blocks, murmurs, coronary artery occlusion patterns are tested as application MCQs.

sequence: Human Heart Anatomy, Blood Flow & Cardiac Physiology for NEET
output.why: Single cohesive subject for NEET preparation; all concepts are interdependent (flow sequence requires chambers, valves, vessels; physiology requires anatomy) and studied together in one NCERT chapter. Splitting would fragment the integrated mental model needed for both diagram labeling and theory MCQs.

exclusions.topic: Fetal circulation and shunts (foramen ovale, ductus arteriosus)
exclusions.consequence: Cannot answer NEET questions on fetal-to-adult transition or congenital shunt physiology; these appear occasionally in previous-year papers.
exclusions.when_to_learn: During reproductive biology or developmental biology modules, or as a dedicated NEET revision addendum.

exclusions.consequence: Missed if a diagram-based MCQ asks about cardiac lymphatics; rare but documented in past papers.
exclusions.when_to_learn: If it appears in a mock test analysis, or during lymphatic system chapter.

exclusions.topic: Detailed molecular mechanisms of cardiac contraction (sliding filament, calcium-induced calcium release)
exclusions.consequence: Unable to answer mechanism-level physiology MCQs that go beyond pressure-volume loops.
exclusions.when_to_learn: In muscle physiology or cell biology modules; not required for standard NEET heart questions.

covered.why: Must label pericardial layers, sinuses, and heart position in mediastinum diagrams; tested in every NEET cycle.

Aortic vestibule, papillary muscles (anterolateral/posteromedial), thick wall, and trabeculae are tested in diagrams and wall-thickness comparison questions.

Three semilunar cusps (right/left/posterior), coronary ostia origins, and aortic sinuses are tested in diagrams and clinical correlate questions.
Annuli fibrosi anchor valves and provide electrical insulation; theory MCQs test its role in separating atrial/ventricular conduction.
SVC, IVC, and coronary sinus openings into RA are fundamental for blood flow tracing and posterior heart labeling.
Pulmonary trunk bifurcation into left/right pulmonary arteries is a key flow pathway step and labeling item in anterior views.
Four pulmonary veins entering LA (two left, two right) tested in labeling and flow sequence questions.
Ascending aorta, arch, and three major branches (brachiocephalic, left common carotid, left subclavian) appear in diagrams and flow tracing.
RCA, LCA, LAD, LCX dominance patterns and supply areas are high-yield theory and occasional diagram items; clinical correlates depend on this.
Coronary sinus drainage into RA is a specific labeling point in posterior/inferior heart views.
Core competency: tracing deoxygenated → oxygenated pathway through all chambers, valves, and vessels is the primary stated target capability.
SA node, AV node, Bundle of His, bundle branches, Purkinje fiber locations and functions are standard theory and occasional diagram items.

covered.concept: Cardiac cycle phases and pressure changes
covered.why: Pressure-volume loops, valve open/close timing, and phase definitions (isovolumetric contraction/relaxation, ejection, filling) are high-yield theory for NEET.
S1/S2 correlation with AV and semilunar valve closure tested in theory MCQs; links to cardiac cycle phases.

covered.concept: Autonomic regulation of heart rate and contractility
covered.why: Sympathetic/parasympathetic effects on SA/AV nodes and contractility are theory staples; mechanism questions appear regularly.
Heart blocks, murmurs, coronary artery occlusion patterns tested as application MCQs; high-yield facts only, not deep pathophysiology.

modules.title: Human Heart Anatomy, Blood Flow & Cardiac Physiology for NEET
covers: Cardiac cycle phases and pressure changes
Autonomic regulation of heart rate and contractility
modules.why_here: All 25 in-play concepts form a single integrated NEET heart chapter. Anatomy concepts (gross, chambers, valves, vessels, coronary) build the structural foundation; blood flow sequence integrates them into the core construct target; physiology concepts (conduction, cycle, sounds, ECG, hemodynamics, autonomic, clinical) complete the theory coverage. They are taught together in NCERT, tested together in NEET, and depend on each other (flow needs anatomy; physiology needs flow/valves). One module matches the single-exam, single-sitting preparation context.
modules.capability: Label all heart anatomy diagrams (external features, internal chambers, valve apparatus, major vessels, coronary circulation) in anterior/posterior/cross-sectional views; trace the complete systemic-to-pulmonary blood flow sequence through every chamber, valve, and vessel; solve NEET-level theory MCQs on cardiac conduction, cardiac cycle phases with pressure changes, heart sound-valve correlations, ECG wave-conduction mapping, cardiac output calculations, autonomic regulation effects, and high-yield clinical correlates (heart blocks, murmurs, coronary occlusion patterns).
